call_points.text: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% with EBITDA margin around 25%, reiterated.
Foundry running about a month late, expected to finish in October.
Sold 1,406 machines in Q1FY27 versus 1,117 a year ago; entry-level mix rose.
Debt at March levels; operating cash flow guided at close to 50% of EBITDA.
Huron export-licence delays tied to geopolitical situation; no near-term resolution seen.
CNC controller commercialisation expected in about two years; PLI application filed.
Debt increased by ~₹300 Cr during the year, primarily incurred for the new capacity expansion.
No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management only says domestic demand outlook remains strong.
Borrowings rose; finance cost rose to ₹69.8 Cr from ₹42.1 Cr.

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Industrial Manufacturing > Industrial Products

operating_notes.text: Order book at 31 March 2026 was ₹4,732 Cr, with Q4FY26 intake of ₹703 Cr and General Engineering the largest segment at 38%.
Installed capacity is 6,000 machines p.a. in India, with a further 10,000 machines p.a. due by September 2026.
FY26 consolidated revenue includes a ~₹67 Cr reversal at Huron subsidiary under the Percentage of Completion Method, described as a deferment to future periods.
Commissioner (Appeal), Central GST & Excise, Rajkot set aside a ₹4,45,59,720 GST demand; the company says it is eligible for a refund of amounts paid under protest.
Q4 FY26 order intake exceeded ₹700 Cr, and order book stood at ₹4,732 Cr.
Capacity utilisation was 86% in Q1FY27 against 6,000 machines a year.
Blended realisation per machine was about ₹34.56 lakh in Q1FY27 versus ₹34.41 lakh a year ago.
Huron capacity is 240 machines, about €75 million (₹750 Cr) at full utilisation.
Crisil assigned Crisil A+/Stable to long-term bank facilities of ₹1,415 Cr and Crisil A1 to short-term bank facilities.

timeline.summary: Jyoti International LLP, via Vikramsinh R. Rana, confirmed no encumbrances on Jyoti CNC Automation shares during FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹599.16 Cr (+4.1% YoY), net profit ₹90.57 Cr (-16.9% YoY).

Jyoti CNC's Q4 & FY26 investor presentation showed FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,093.1 Cr (+15.2% YoY) and PAT of ₹336.0 Cr (+6.3%), with Q4 PAT down 16.9% on a ~₹67 Cr revenue reversal at Huron subsidiary; order book ₹4,732 Cr at 31 March 2026.

Bharatkuma Gandhi submitted the recording of the May 29, 2026, conference call per SEBI Regulation 30, available at **https://jyoti.co.in/investors/announcements/investor-meet-and-related-disclosures/**.
2026-05-31: Commissioner (Appeal), Central GST & Excise, Rajkot set aside a ₹4.46 Cr GST demand on Jyoti CNC; the company says it is now eligible for a refund of amounts paid under protest.
Jyoti CNC reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue of ₹599 Cr and noted a ₹67 Cr revenue deferment at Huron due to export investigations.
Crisil assigned Crisil A+/Stable and Crisil A1 ratings to ₹1,415 Cr bank facilities on 16 October 2026.
